title: Millions of Souls, in Glory Now
description: Millions of Souls, in Glory Now in Tonic Solfa to YORK, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 3 verses and a piano.
about: Philip Doddridge wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 688 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Room at the Lord's Table”.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Common Metre (8.6.8.6), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to YORK; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: Mil-lions of souls, in glo-ry now, Were fed and feast-ed here; And mil-lions more, still on the way, A-round the board ap-pear.

lines: Millions of souls, in glory now,
And millions more, still on the way,
Yet is his house and heart so large
Nor could the whole assembled world
All things are ready; come away,
Crowd to your places at the feast,

licence: Public domain: Philip Doddridge died in 1751.
credits: Words by Philip Doddridge (1702–1751), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to YORK by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
